questions.question: Forward Bloc was founded in 1939-40 by which of the following leaders?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Subhash Chandra Bose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose** was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who played a key role in India's independence movement.
 
• He founded the **Forward Bloc** in **1939** after resigning from the Indian National Congress due to ideological differences with its leadership.
 
• The Forward Bloc was established with the aim to bring together all **left-wing and nationalist forces** in India to fight against British colonial rule.
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose was deeply influenced by the ideas of socialism and sought to create a mass revolutionary movement.
 
• The Forward Bloc emphasized principles such as **self-reliance, socialism, secularism, and anti-colonialism.**
 
• It played a significant role in the struggle for independence, particularly in mobilizing the youth and workers for the cause.
 
• Bose later became the leader of the **Indian National Army (INA)** and launched an armed struggle against the British during World War II.
 
• He is famously known for his slogan **"Give me blood, and I will give you freedom."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rash Behari Bose**__

 __
 
• **Rash Behari Bose** was another prominent revolutionary who played a significant role in India's independence struggle.
 
• He was instrumental in the **Ghadar Movement** and later became associated with the Indian National Army (INA).
 
• He was one of the founding leaders of the INA but handed over its leadership to **Subhash Chandra Bose.**
 
• While Rash Behari Bose was a key figure in the freedom movement, he did not establish the Forward Bloc.
 
 
 
• **Jawahar Lal Nehru**__
 __
 
• **Jawahar Lal Nehru** was India's first Prime Minister and a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He played a central role in shaping modern India's policies and promoting ideas of **secularism, socialism, and democratic governance.**
 
• Nehru was associated with the Congress Party and its leadership rather than founding separate organizations like the Forward Bloc.
 
 
 
• **Chittaranjan Das**__
 
 
• **Chittaranjan Das**, popularly known as Deshbandhu, was a prominent nationalist leader and lawyer.
 
• He played a key role in the **Non-Cooperation Movement** and was a mentor to Subhash Chandra Bose.
 
• Chittaranjan Das was associated with the Swaraj Party but not with the establishment of the Forward Bloc.

questions.question: On which of the following dates did the British Empire transfer its powers to the Constituent Assembly in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15th August**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On **15th August 1947**, the British Empire officially transferred its powers to the Constituent Assembly of India.
 
• This date marked the **independence of India** from British colonial rule after nearly 200 years.
 
• The Constituent Assembly, formed in **December 1946**, was responsible for drafting India's Constitution and taking over governance.
 
• Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last Viceroy of India, oversaw the transition of power to Indian leaders.
 
• India became a **sovereign, democratic nation** with the transfer of power on this historic day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly**

 
 
• The Constituent Assembly of India was established under the **Cabinet Mission Plan** of 1946.
 
• It consisted of representatives elected by the provincial legislatures and nominated by princely states.
 
• The Assembly was responsible for drafting the Constitution, which was adopted on **26th November 1949**.
 
 
 
• **Independence Act of 1947**
 
 
• The British Parliament passed the **Indian Independence Act of 1947**, leading to the partition of British India into India and Pakistan.
 
• The Act also declared that power would be transferred to the newly formed governments on **15th August 1947**.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India**
 
 
• The independence of India was accompanied by the partition, dividing British India into **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• This led to significant migration and communal violence during the transition period.
 
 
 
• **National Symbols**
 
 
• The **Tricolour Flag** was officially adopted on 22nd July 1947, prior to independence.
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** delivered the famous "Tryst with Destiny" speech on the eve of independence.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters gave the famous quote "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!" ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhash Chandra Bose.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose:-**

 
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose was an Indian revolutionary who played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was born in 1897 in Cuttack, Odisha, and he was educated at the University of Calcutta.
 
• After graduating, Bose worked as a civil servant, but he soon resigned from his job to devote himself to the independence movement.
 
• Bose was a prominent Indian nationalist who believed in **using force** to achieve independence from British rule.
 
• He was the founder of the **Indian National Army,** which fought alongside the **Japanese during World War II.**
 
• He gave the famous quote "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!".
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel** was another prominent freedom fighter who played a key role in** India's struggle for independence.**

 
 
• He was known as the** "Iron Man of India" **for his leadership in unifying the country after independence.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:-**
 
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, popularly known as Lokmanya Tilak, was an Indian nationalist, freedom fighter, lawyer, and social reformer.
 
• He was one of the first and strongest advocates of Swaraj (self-rule) and a strong radical in Indian consciousness.
 
• He is known for his quote in Marathi: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!".
 
 
 
• ​** Lala Lajpat Rai:-**
 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai, also known as the Lion of Punjab, was a prominent Indian freedom fighter, lawyer, and author.
 
• He was one of the three leaders of the Lal-Bal-Pal triumvirate in the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: Lala Lajpat Rai was an active member of which organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was an active member of **Arya Samaj,** a Hindu reformist movement that aimed to promote the principles o**f Vedas **and to oppose the** caste system and idol worship.**
 
• He was also one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress** and played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Arya Samaj is regarded as a **monotheistic Indian Hindu reform movement** that upholds **moral principles and ethical behavior **in accordance with the conviction that the Vedas are **infallible. **
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati,** an austere sannyasi, founded the samaj in the** 1870s.**
 
• The first Hindu group to introduce **proselytization** inside **Hinduism **was Arya Samaj.
 
• Since the 1800s, the group has also campaigned to **advance the civil rights struggle** in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj** was another** Hindu reformist movement **founded by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 **that aimed to promote monotheism and social reform.
 
• **Brahmo Sabha** was an earlier version of **Brahmo Samaj founded in 1828** that later split into different factions.
 
• **Prathana Sabha** was a religious society founded by **Keshub Chandra Sen,** a disciple of **Raja Ram Mohan Roy, in 1867** that aimed to promote social and religious reform.

questions.question: During which freedom struggle movement, Mahatma Gandhi Ji gave the call for "Do or Die"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India movement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi Ji** gave the call for **"Do or Die"** during the **Quit India movement.**
 
• The Quit India movement was launched on **8th August 1942**, demanding the immediate** end of British rule** in India.
 
• The movement was a **mass civil disobedience campaign**, and the slogan "Do or Die" was meant to **inspire people** to fight for their freedom.
 
• The movement was **suppressed** by the British authorities, and many leaders including Mahatma Gandhi Ji were **arrested.**
 
• The Quit India movement played a significant role in **India's struggle for independence, **and it was a turning point in India's history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Khilafat movement:**

 
 
• The Khilafat movement was launched in** 1919** to** protest against the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire** and the **abolition of the caliphate.**
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi Ji** supported the movement and it helped to **unite the Muslims and Hindus** in India.
 
 
 
• **Non-cooperation movement:**
 
 
• The Non-cooperation movement was launched in **1920** to **boycott British goods and institutions.**
 
• Mahatma Gandhi Ji called off the movement in **1922** after the **Chauri Chaura incident.**
 
 
 
• **Dandi March:**
 
 
• The Dandi March was a salt march led by Mahatma Gandhi Ji in **1930** to protest against the British salt tax.
 
• The march lasted for **24 days** and covered a distance of **240 miles.**
 
• It was a significant event in** India's struggle for independence.**

questions.question: In which of the following years was the 'Quit India Movement' launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1942**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on **8 August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• Gandhi delivered the iconic "Do or Die" speech at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The movement is also known as the **August Kranti** or August Movement.
 
• The British responded with mass arrests and repression, detaining many leaders of the Indian National Congress without trial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World War II Context**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement occurred during the turbulent times of World War II, when British resources were stretched thin.
 
• India's contribution to the British war effort was significant, which led to increasing demands for self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Arrest of Leaders**
 
 
• Following the launch of the movement, the British arrested nearly all leaders of the Indian National Congress, including Gandhi, Nehru, and Patel.
 
• This led to a leaderless movement, which saw widespread but uncoordinated protests across the country.
 
 
 
• **Public Response**
 
 
• Despite the lack of central leadership, the movement saw massive public participation, including strikes, protests, and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• The British government responded with severe repression, including police violence, mass detentions, and press censorship.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Independence**
 
 
• Though the Quit India Movement was ultimately suppressed, it significantly intensified the Indian struggle for independence.
 
• It demonstrated the Indian population's unified demand for freedom, which played a crucial role in the eventual British decision to leave India in 1947.

questions.question: Who founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhas Chandra Bose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party.
 
• The All-India Forward Bloc was formed on **3rd May 1939**, as a faction within the Indian National Congress.
 
• Bose aimed to consolidate the political left and to rally all radical elements within the Congress under one banner.
 
• He sought to establish a socialist state in India and believed in armed struggle against British colonial rule.
 
• The Forward Bloc played a significant role in the Indian independence movement, especially during the Quit India Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was a prominent freedom fighter and a nationalist leader who advocated for complete independence from British rule.
 
• He was elected as the President of the Indian National Congress twice, in **1938** and **1939**.
 
• After differences with Mahatma Gandhi and other Congress leaders, Bose resigned from the Congress presidency and formed the Forward Bloc.
 
• He later went on to lead the Indian National Army (INA) to fight against the British during World War II.
 
• Bose's legacy continues to be remembered and honored in India for his uncompromising patriotism and his efforts towards India's independence.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Syed Ahmed Khan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan:-**__

 __
 
• He was a Muslim scholar, social reformer, and educationalist in British India.
 
• He was one of the first Muslim intellectuals to argue that Hindus and Muslims were two distinct nations with different cultures and values.
 
• He believed that Muslims could not prosper in a united India dominated by Hindus, and that they needed a separate homeland where they could practice their religion and culture freely.
 
• **He is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory". (Hence option 2 is correct)**
 
• Khan's two-nation theory was later adopted by the Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• The Muslim League campaigned for the creation of a separate Muslim state in British India, which eventually led to the partition of India and the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian anti-colonial nationalist, secular humanist, social democrat, and author who was a central figure in India during the middle of the 20th century.
 
• **Nehru was a principal leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s. Upon India's independence in 1947, he served as the country's first prime minister for 17 years. **
 
• Nehru promoted parliamentary democracy, secularism, and science and technology during the 1950s, powerfully influencing India's arc as a modern nation.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:-**
 
 
• **He was one of the pioneers of the Indian independence movement. He is considered the "Father of Indian Unrest" by the British.**
 
• Tilak was a staunch nationalist and believed that India should be independent from British rule.
 
• He was a leading figure in the Swadeshi movement, which promoted the use of Indian-made goods instead of British goods.
 
• He also founded the Home Rule League, which demanded self-government for India.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah:-**
 
 
• **He was a Pakistani barrister, politician and statesman who is widely regarded as the founder of Pakistan.**
 
• Jinnah was initially a member of the Indian National Congress (INC), but he became disillusioned with the party's secular policies. He believed that Muslims needed their own political party to represent their interests.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India revived the Indian National Army ‘Azad Hind Fauj’ (which was formed in 1942 by Rash Behari Bose and Captain-General Mohan Singh) in the year 1943?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Subhas Chandra Bose__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Azad Hind Fauj or the India National Army (INA) was first established by Mohan Singh in 1942.

 
 
• It was revived by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose on October 21, 1943, during the Second World War to secure India’s complete independence from British Raj.
 
• On this day, India’s first independent provisional government named Azad Hind Government was announced.
 
• This was followed by a conference in Bangkok (June 1942), where Rashbehari Bose was elected president of the league and a decision was taken to raise the Indian National Army.
 
• Captain Mohan Singh was appointed the commander of the INA, which had about 40,000 Indian soldiers
 
• This conference invited Bose to lead the movement.
 
 
• Earlier, Bose had escaped from India in 1941 to Berlin.
 
• In June 1943 he came to Tokyo and then India joined the INA in Singapore.
 
 
 
• Rashbehari Bose handed over the leadership to Subhas Bose, and an Azad Hind Sarkar was formed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:**

 
 
• **​**He was born on 2 October 1869.
 
• He started his political career in South Africa where he launched a Civil Disobedience Movement against the maltreatment meted out to Asian settlers.
 
• In 1915, he returned to India and took up the leadership of the National Freedom Struggle.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi led the national freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• Gandhiji launched many movements to force the British to concede India its Independence.
 
• The well-known being is Non-Co-operation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), and the Quit India Movement (1942).
 
• Gandhi wrote his famous autobiography under the title 'My Experiments with Truth'.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi is better known as the father of the Nation.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of free India between 15 August 1947 – 27 May 1964.
 
• He was also one of the principal leaders of India’s independence movement in the 1930s and ’40s.
 
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh:**
 
 
• **​**Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were involved in the Lahore conspiracy case and because of this, the court had ordered that they were to be hanged on March 23, 1931.
 
• March 23 was the day of execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru is observed as the Shaheed Diwas in India every year so as a show of respect for its revolutionary heroes.
 
• Three of them were involved in the killing of John Saunders, a British cop who was believed to have thrashed Lala Lajpatpat Rai.
 
• They were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• Bhagat Singh along with Batukeshwar Dutt threw a harmless bomb in the Central Legislative assembly to protest the passing of the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.
 
• Bhagat Singh popularized the phrase " Inqualab Zindabad" which was first phrased by Maulana Hazrat Mohani.
 
• Some of the books written by Bhagat Singh are "Why I Am an Atheist", "No Hanging, Please Shoot Us", "on the Path of Liberation" among others.
